openspec/specs/car-control-api/spec.md

car control api

car-control-api Specification

Purpose

Defines how controllers request car motion, acquire ownership, arm, stop and inspect capabilities and status consistently across the supported transports.

Requirements

Setpoint

The car's device control API SHALL accept a setpoint as a geometry_msgs/TwistStamped, using linear.x and linear.y in m/s and angular.z in rad/s, in base_link. A setpoint with any other Twist component non-zero SHALL be rejected and not applied. An owner's fresh, finite planar setpoint whose absolute linear.x, linear.y or angular.z exceeds its capability limit SHALL raise a safety stop.

Out-of-plane setpoint is rejected
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends a setpoint with linear.z = 0.1
  • THEN the setpoint is not applied and does not renew the lease
  • AND no safety stop is raised
Out-of-limits setpoint stops the car
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends a setpoint with linear.x above the capabilities' maximum
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason out-of-limits

Mecanum kinematics

The car SHALL use mecanum_drive_controller inverse kinematics and parameter names, divide wheel-speed references by configured max_wheel_speed, and clamp to −1.0..=1.0. The current geometry SHALL use radius 0.030 m and centre projection sum 0.1275 m, with zero frame offset. The profile's 40 rad/s normalization and 1/1/3 input limits are experimental values, not measured physical maxima; speed tracking is approximate (O2).

Same result as mecanum_drive_controller
  • GIVEN a wheels_radius, sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis and max_wheel_speed
  • WHEN the car is armed and applies a setpoint
  • THEN each wheel command (FL, FR, RR, RL) equals its inverse-kinematic wheel speed divided by max_wheel_speed, clamped independently to −1.0..=1.0
Same input on every source gives the same wheel commands
  • GIVEN the same setpoint
  • WHEN it is sent by an armed owner over BLE, UDP and ROS 2 in turn
  • THEN the wheel commands are identical
Combined inputs saturate independently
  • GIVEN radius 0.03 m, zero frame offset, normalization 40 rad/s and input limits allowing vx=1 and vy=1
  • WHEN the armed owner sends vx=1, vy=1, wz=0
  • THEN normalized commands are (0, 1, 0, 1), not (0, 1.667, 0, 1.667)

Open-loop motion references

Twist fields SHALL retain their standard m/s and rad/s meaning as requested motion references. Product documentation SHALL describe current open-loop tracking as approximate and link the M5 observations. The car SHALL NOT present command-derived speed as measured velocity or promise velocity accuracy without supporting evidence.

An estimate is not measured feedback
  • GIVEN the current motors have no encoders and only short-pulse observations are available
  • WHEN the product describes speed or publishes status
  • THEN observed motion estimates are identified as approximate
  • AND commanded velocity is not presented as measured feedback

Latest setpoint wins

The car SHALL apply only the owner's latest setpoint, with no queue. A setpoint whose sequence is not newer than the last accepted one SHALL NOT be applied.

Older sequence is ignored
  • GIVEN the current BLE/UDP session, or one ROS publisher, last accepted setpoint sequence 10
  • WHEN a setpoint with sequence 9 or 10 arrives
  • THEN it is not applied and does not renew the lease

Single owner

The first controller to claim SHALL become the owner. Other controllers' claims SHALL be refused and their control input ignored. Repeated UDP HELLO from the current owner SHALL return its existing session without renewing deadlines. BLE ownership SHALL disable the AP; UDP or ROS ownership SHALL stop BLE advertising. UDP and ROS share the AP and SHALL exclude one another through ownership checks, not radio shutdown.

Second claimant is refused
  • GIVEN a UDP controller owns the car
  • WHEN a second UDP controller sends a hello
  • THEN it receives BUSY
  • AND the owner is unchanged
Other radio is off while owned
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a BLE controller connects
  • THEN it becomes the owner and the car AP goes off
  • AND when ownership is released, BLE advertising and the car AP are both up
Non-owner ROS node is ignored
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 node owns the car
  • WHEN another node publishes a setpoint or an arm
  • THEN it is ignored
UDP and ROS share the Wi-Fi radio
  • GIVEN a UDP owner and a connected ROS router on the car AP
  • WHEN a ROS node sends a setpoint
  • THEN the AP stays up, the setpoint cannot claim or drive, and the UDP lease is unchanged
  • AND the same exclusion applies to UDP input while a ROS node owns the car

Claim window

If the owner sends no valid setpoint within the claim window, ownership SHALL be released.

Silent owner loses the car
  • GIVEN a controller has just claimed the car
  • WHEN the claim window passes with no valid setpoint from it
  • THEN ownership is released and every radio reopens

Explicit arming

New owners SHALL start disarmed. BLE/UDP SHALL require the owner's explicit arm and a valid lease. ROS SHALL auto-arm on an owner's valid setpoint only after a claim or lease expiry (ADR-0011). After STOP or out-of-limits, all sources SHALL require a fresh setpoint followed by explicit arm. Disarmed setpoints SHALL renew the lease while wheel commands remain zero.

Setpoints alone do not move the car
  • GIVEN a new BLE or UDP owner that has not armed
  • WHEN it streams non-zero setpoints
  • THEN every wheel command is zero
Arm without a lease is refused
  • GIVEN a new BLE or UDP owner that has sent no setpoint
  • WHEN it sends arm
  • THEN arm is refused with not-ready and the car stays disarmed
A ROS 2 stream arms the car
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a known ROS 2 node streams valid non-zero setpoints on /cmd_vel and nothing on /rovi/arm
  • THEN the first setpoint claims and arms the car and the wheel commands follow it
  • AND after a lease expiry, the resumed stream arms the car again
A ROS 2 stop stays latched while streaming
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 owner that is streaming and armed
  • WHEN it publishes /rovi/arm false and keeps streaming
  • THEN the car stops and every wheel command stays zero until the owner publishes /rovi/arm true
Arm then drive
  • GIVEN an owner with a fresh valid setpoint, a valid lease and valid motor configuration
  • WHEN it sends arm, then a non-zero setpoint
  • THEN the car is armed and the wheel commands follow the setpoint
Arm after a stop needs a new setpoint
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop while its lease was valid
  • WHEN it sends arm before any new setpoint
  • THEN arm is refused with not-ready and the car stays in safety stop
  • AND after one valid setpoint, the next arm succeeds

Lease and watchdog timeout

Only the owner's valid setpoints SHALL renew the lease. When the lease expires, the car SHALL raise a watchdog timeout and a safety stop within the lease length plus 50 ms (M8's acceptance bound), checked by the control tick independently of incoming traffic.

Silent armed owner is stopped
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN no valid setpoint arrives for longer than the lease
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason lease-expired, within the lease plus 50 ms
  • AND every wheel command is zero

Safety stop

STOP, lease expiry, owner loss and out-of-limits SHALL zero wheel commands, put both drivers in standby and disarm. Ownership SHALL be retained except on owner loss or window expiry. STOP/out-of-limits SHALL require a fresh valid setpoint then explicit ARM. Lease expiry SHALL allow ROS auto-arm on a fresh valid setpoint; BLE/UDP SHALL still require explicit ARM. Release SHALL clear session state while keeping drivers disabled.

Stop keeps the owner
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends stop
  • THEN the car is in safety stop with reason stop, disarmed, with every driver in standby
  • AND the controller is still the owner
Owner loss while armed
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner disconnects or sends bye
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason owner-lost
  • AND ownership is released
Further setpoints do not clear the latch
  • GIVEN the car stopped because of STOP or out-of-limits
  • WHEN the owner streams valid setpoints without explicit ARM
  • THEN every wheel command stays zero

Reclaim window

After a stop or an out-of-limits setpoint, the owner SHALL be kept for as long as its valid setpoints keep the lease valid. The reclaim window SHALL start when the lease lapses: at once on a lease expiry, or when the owner goes quiet after a stop or an out-of-limits setpoint. Within the window, the owner SHALL be able to resume in the same session using the explicit/automatic arming rules. When the window ends, ownership SHALL be released.

Streaming owner is kept after a stop
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop
  • WHEN it keeps streaming valid setpoints for longer than the reclaim window
  • THEN it is still the owner and the car stays in safety stop
Quiet owner after a stop is released
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop
  • WHEN it sends no setpoint after that
  • THEN the reclaim window starts when its lease lapses
  • AND ownership is released when the window ends, and every radio reopens
Out-of-limits keeps a streaming owner
  • GIVEN an out-of-limits setpoint raised a safety stop
  • WHEN the owner keeps streaming valid setpoints and then sends arm
  • THEN the car is armed in the same session
Resume within the window
  • GIVEN the car stopped on lease expiry
  • WHEN the same owner sends a valid setpoint and arm within the reclaim window
  • THEN the car is armed in the same session
Window ends
  • GIVEN the car stopped on lease expiry
  • WHEN the reclaim window passes without explicit or permitted automatic arming
  • THEN ownership is released and every radio reopens

Boot state

After power-up or reset, the car SHALL be open, with no owner, disarmed, every wheel command zero and every driver in standby.

Fresh boot
  • GIVEN the car has just booted
  • WHEN a controller reads the status
  • THEN the state is open
  • AND the car log reports every wheel command as zero

Capabilities

The car SHALL give its capabilities on every source: protocol version, wheels_radius, sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis, maximum linear.x, linear.y and angular.z, lease length, claim window and reclaim window. BLE (Capabilities characteristic) and UDP (HELLO_ACK) give them to the owner on claim; ROS 2 gives them before the claim, as below. Each value SHALL be the one the car enforces, so a controller needs no hardcoded limits.

Limits match enforcement
  • GIVEN a controller has read the capabilities
  • WHEN it sends a setpoint at exactly the maximum linear.x
  • THEN the setpoint is applied
  • AND a setpoint above it raises a safety stop
Same capabilities on every source
  • GIVEN the same car
  • WHEN a BLE, a UDP and a ROS 2 controller each read the capabilities
  • THEN every value is identical

ROS 2 capabilities topic

A ROS 2 controller claims with its first setpoint, so ROS 2 SHALL give the capabilities without a claim. The car SHALL publish them on /rovi/capabilities as std_msgs/String of space-separated key=value pairs, latched: reliable, transient local, depth 1. O9 selects this QoS or the specified volatile fallback; the published values are identical in both modes.

Late subscriber gets the capabilities
  • GIVEN the car is open and connected to the ROS 2 router
  • WHEN a node starts and subscribes to /rovi/capabilities
  • THEN it receives the capabilities without sending anything to the car
One pair per field
  • GIVEN a node has received /rovi/capabilities
  • WHEN it splits the string on spaces and =
  • THEN it gets exactly one value for every key in the capabilities encoding requirement
Reading the capabilities is not a claim
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a ROS 2 node reads /rovi/capabilities
  • THEN the car stays open and every radio stays up

ROS 2 capabilities republish fallback

If O9 shows that zenoh-nostd cannot serve transient-local late joiners, the car SHALL use reliable, volatile, depth-1 capabilities and republish at least once per second and on every claim, release and router reconnect. Controllers SHALL subscribe with volatile durability in fallback mode. Documentation SHALL identify the chosen mode; the car SHALL NOT advertise unsupported transient-local durability.

Late subscriber gets the capabilities without latching
  • GIVEN the car uses the republish fallback
  • WHEN a node with compatible volatile QoS subscribes while the car is open and the router is healthy
  • THEN it receives the capabilities within one second

Status

The car SHALL report its status to the owner on every source (BLE Status characteristic, UDP STATUS, ROS 2 /rovi/status): state (open, claimed, armed or stopped), stop reason (none, stop, lease-expired, owner-lost or out-of-limits) and last owner control error (none, not-ready or invalid). Status SHALL be readable at once after a claim. Every status read or notification SHALL report the state at that moment.

Status follows a stop
  • GIVEN the car is armed and the owner reads status
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the next status reports safety stop with reason lease-expired
Readable right after the claim
  • GIVEN a BLE controller has just connected
  • WHEN it reads Status before any other write
  • THEN the status reports claimed with no error

ROS 2 status topic

The car SHALL publish /rovi/status as std_msgs/String of space-separated key=value pairs with the same content as the other sources' status: state (open, claimed, armed or stopped), reason (none except while stopped), error (none when clear) and session (decimal u32, 0 while open). It SHALL publish on every change of any of these and at least once a second, so a late subscriber sees the current status within a second.

Stop reason on ROS 2
  • GIVEN the car is armed under a ROS 2 owner
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the next /rovi/status has state=stopped and reason=lease-expired
Refused arm on ROS 2
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 owner stopped by its own STOP
  • WHEN it publishes arm before any new setpoint
  • THEN the next /rovi/status has state=stopped and error=not-ready
Status on a change
  • GIVEN a node subscribed to /rovi/status
  • WHEN the state changes
  • THEN it receives the new status without waiting for the next periodic publish

Last command error

On every source, a refused owner control command (ARM/STOP; not-ready or invalid) SHALL persist as the last error until the owner's next successful control command. Setpoints and echo SHALL NOT clear it. New sessions SHALL start with no error. Non-owner or old-session input SHALL NOT change it. BUSY is a response to a claimant, not an owner-status error.

Refused arm shows on every source
  • GIVEN a BLE, UDP or ROS owner that sent STOP and has sent no valid setpoint since
  • WHEN it sends explicit ARM
  • THEN the status reports the last command error not-ready
  • AND a later setpoint does not clear it, and a successful arm does
Non-owner commands do not change the owner's status
  • GIVEN an owner whose status reports no error
  • WHEN another controller sends arm
  • THEN the owner's status still reports no error

Input validation before state changes

Malformed framing/CDR, non-finite Twist components, non-planar Twist, invalid Bool/control payloads, and unknown ROS publishers SHALL NOT claim, renew a lease, change outputs or consume a setpoint sequence. An identifiable owner's invalid control payload SHALL report invalid; invalid setpoint/framing SHALL be discarded. Owner/session and sequence checks SHALL precede limit enforcement, so an intruder or stale packet cannot stop the car.

Invalid setpoint leaves the stream intact
  • GIVEN an armed owner with last sequence 10
  • WHEN sequence 11 contains NaN or truncated CDR
  • THEN the previous output and lease deadline stay unchanged
  • AND a later valid sequence 11 can be accepted
Stale or non-owner oversized input cannot stop the owner
  • GIVEN an armed owner with last sequence 10
  • WHEN sequence 9 from that owner, or input from a non-owner, exceeds a velocity limit
  • THEN it is ignored without changing the state or renewing the lease
Bad first ROS input does not claim
  • GIVEN the car is open and a known ROS publisher
  • WHEN it sends a non-finite or out-of-limits setpoint
  • THEN the car stays open and disabled

Setpoint frame and time interpretation

Empty frame_id SHALL mean base_link; base_link SHALL be accepted. Other frame names SHALL be rejected because the car does not transform frames. CDR strings SHALL be valid UTF-8, NUL-terminated and at most 64 bytes excluding the terminator. Receive time SHALL govern leases; the header stamp SHALL NOT substitute for a synchronized clock. A timestamp with nanoseconds outside 0..999999999 SHALL be rejected.

Unsupported frame does not drive
  • GIVEN an armed owner
  • WHEN it sends an otherwise valid twist in map
  • THEN the sample is discarded without lease renewal or sequence consumption
Unsynchronized stamp is not a freshness clock
  • GIVEN a valid owner and a newer setpoint sequence
  • WHEN a supported-frame setpoint arrives with an old or zero header timestamp
  • THEN it is accepted using the local receive time for its lease

Sequence domains

BLE/UDP setpoint sequences SHALL use u32 serial ordering: newer iff wrapping difference is in 1..2^31-1; equal and exactly-half-range values SHALL be dropped. ROS SHALL compare full nonnegative i64 attachment sequences strictly increasingly per publisher GID, independently for setpoint and arm publishers. Sequence history SHALL reset with the session; accepted messages from distinct owner publishers SHALL be ordered by receipt, never by comparing their counters.

BLE or UDP counter wraps
  • GIVEN last setpoint sequence 4294967295
  • WHEN sequence 0 arrives in the same session
  • THEN it is newer; a subsequent 4294967295 is stale
Same-node publishers have independent counters
  • GIVEN an owner node with setpoint publisher A at sequence 100 and publisher B with no accepted sample
  • WHEN B sends sequence 1, then A repeats sequence 100
  • THEN B's setpoint is accepted and A's duplicate is dropped
  • AND an arm publisher's own sequence 1 is not compared with either setpoint counter

Session isolation and ROS identity

UDP identity SHALL include peer address/port and the current session ID; BLE identity SHALL include the connection lifetime, not a reusable handle alone. ROS ownership SHALL use graph-announced node identity (zid/nid), not publisher GID; unknown publishers SHALL be ignored. Release or adapter reconnect SHALL discard its queued old-generation input and ordering state. Stale UDP session IDs and callbacks from closed BLE connections SHALL be ignored.

Old UDP traffic cannot affect a new claim
  • GIVEN the same peer has released session S and claimed session T
  • WHEN a delayed ARM, STOP or setpoint with session S arrives
  • THEN ownership, state, lease and last error for T remain unchanged
An arm publisher belongs to the owning node
  • GIVEN cmd_vel and arm publishers announced under one node, with distinct GIDs
  • WHEN that node owns the car and sends a valid explicit ARM with a fresh lease
  • THEN ARM succeeds; an unannounced publisher or another node cannot arm it
Router disconnect ends an owning ROS session
  • GIVEN a ROS owner and queued adapter input
  • WHEN the adapter detects router disconnection
  • THEN owner loss stops and releases the car, old queued input is discarded, and reconnect re-declares endpoints and rebuilds graph identity
  • AND before disconnection is detected, missing setpoints still trigger the independent lease timeout

Motor validation fault integration

A motor-layer validation fault SHALL cause a device out-of-limits safety stop and a diagnostic identifying the internal wheel fault. Both drivers SHALL remain in standby until the owner sends a fresh valid setpoint followed by explicit ARM, on every source including ROS. Repeated control ticks or new valid setpoints alone SHALL NOT re-enable motor control. Invalid boot configuration SHALL prevent motor enable and make ARM fail not-ready.

Internal wheel fault cannot auto-recover
  • GIVEN an armed ROS owner and a fault injected into one computed wheel command
  • WHEN motor control reports the fault
  • THEN the car reports stopped/out-of-limits and both drivers stay disabled
  • AND continued setpoints alone do not resume; a fresh valid setpoint then explicit ARM can recover with a valid configuration

Capabilities encoding

ROS capabilities SHALL contain the nine keys in the scenario below exactly once, with space-separated key=value tokens and locale-independent decimal numbers. Geometry and input limits SHALL describe the same canonical f32 values encoded by BLE/UDP; integer fields SHALL be exact. Field order SHALL be insignificant. A session ID SHALL NOT be a capability; UDP carries it in the frame header.

Keys and units are unambiguous
  • GIVEN a capabilities message
  • WHEN a controller parses it
  • THEN version is an integer protocol version; wheels_radius and sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis are metres
  • AND max_vx and max_vy are m/s, max_wz is rad/s
  • AND lease_ms, claim_ms, reclaim_ms are integer milliseconds
  • AND floats use enough digits to round-trip their canonical f32 values

Status delivery and empty values

BLE SHALL update readable Status immediately on claim and every change, and notify subscribed centrals on changes. UDP SHALL reply STATUS to owner ARM/STOP, including refusals, and send STATUS on a stop transition to its owner; it provides no reliable delivery guarantee. ROS SHALL emit all four status keys on each publication, with reason=none outside stopped and error=none when clear. Release SHALL clear the status reason/error and report open.

Release does not leave a stale reason
  • GIVEN a stopped owner with reason stop and error not-ready
  • WHEN ownership is released
  • THEN readable/published status is open with no reason or error and ROS session=0
  • AND the next claimant starts with no previous-session error

Valid operating profile

Geometry and normalization SHALL be finite and positive; frame offsets SHALL be finite. Input limits SHALL be finite nonnegative f32-representable values, enforced after canonicalizing to the advertised f32 values. Lease and window lengths SHALL be integers in 1..65535 ms. Invalid profiles SHALL fail initialization with drivers disabled rather than advertise truncated values or permit claims. Numerical overflow during valid-input kinematics SHALL trigger motor fault handling.

Invalid normalization fails closed
  • GIVEN max_wheel_speed is zero or NaN, or a lease exceeds 65535 ms
  • WHEN the device initializes
  • THEN initialization reports an error, motor enable is unavailable and control claims are not accepted

Deadline ordering

Before processing control input at time t, the device SHALL process any claim, lease or reclaim deadline at or before t using a monotonic clock. Expired sessions SHALL NOT be revived by queued ARM or setpoint input. After release, BLE/UDP SHALL require a new claim; ROS MAY create a new claim from an otherwise valid sample. Automatic ROS arming SHALL NOT clear an existing STOP/out-of-limits latch before release.

Packet on the reclaim boundary
  • GIVEN a UDP session with reclaim deadline t
  • WHEN its ARM or setpoint arrives at t
  • THEN the old ownership is released first, and that packet cannot drive or renew the expired session

Echo is observational

UDP Echo and the BLE Echo characteristic SHALL return payloads of at most 32 bytes unchanged and discard larger ones. Echo SHALL NOT claim, arm, change wheel commands, renew deadlines, consume setpoint sequences or clear errors. UDP echo SHALL be available to non-owners; BLE connection itself still claims as usual, so BLE echo does not provide a parallel non-owner connection.

Echo does not keep an owner alive
  • GIVEN an owner stops sending setpoints but continues echo probes
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the normal lease stop occurs and ownership eventually expires without ARM

New session allocation

Each new claim SHALL allocate a nonzero session ID; repeated HELLO by the current UDP owner SHALL keep that ID and its deadlines. UDP IDs SHALL be seeded randomly per boot and incremented per new claim, skipping zero on wrap. This SHALL be documented as stale-packet separation, not authentication or a guarantee against deliberate replay. BLE sessions SHALL use connection generations; ROS sessions SHALL use the identity and queue rules above.

Repeated hello does not reset a claim
  • GIVEN a UDP owner in session S with an existing claim or lease deadline
  • WHEN the same peer repeats HELLO
  • THEN HELLO_ACK carries S and the same capabilities, without extending either deadline

Bounded ROS ordering history

The adapter SHALL retain sequence high-water marks for every accepted owner publisher for the current session, including across publisher removal. Other graph announcements SHALL NOT evict those marks. If bounded storage cannot track another owner publisher, its input SHALL be discarded without lease renewal rather than accepted without replay checks. Ownership release SHALL clear these session marks.

Unrelated publishers cannot reset ordering
  • GIVEN an owner publisher whose last accepted sequence is 100
  • WHEN unrelated graph announcements fill the table and that publisher repeats sequence 99
  • THEN sequence 99 is rejected and cannot renew the lease

openspec/specs/laptop-teleoperation/spec.md

laptop teleoperation

laptop-teleoperation Specification

Purpose

Lets a laptop operator control the existing car UDP API interactively with explicit arming, bounded motion input, visible state and predictable failure cleanup.

Requirements

Explicit connection without motion

The client SHALL require an explicit IPv4 target/port and an interactive terminal. It SHALL claim once with version-1 UDP HELLO, validate the returned nonzero session and capabilities, and start locally disarmed with zero intent. BUSY, invalid capabilities or a one-second handshake timeout SHALL fail without ARM or nonzero setpoints. Leases shorter than 200 ms SHALL be reported unsupported.

Connection starts disarmed
  • WHEN an operator connects to a valid target
  • THEN the client displays the negotiated limits and session and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Refused or unsupported connection
  • WHEN the target returns BUSY, invalid capabilities, an unsupported lease, or no valid reply within one second
  • THEN the client reports failure and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint

Explicit arm and stop latch

Only an operator R key SHALL request ARM, after clearing motion and sending a fresh zero setpoint. Motion SHALL remain disabled until a matching successful Armed Status reply arrives. A refused/timed-out ARM, STOP or reported safety stop SHALL clear intent and require a new R key before further motion. Held or repeated motion keys SHALL never arm the car.

Keys cannot arm
  • GIVEN a connected but locally disarmed client
  • WHEN motion keys arrive
  • THEN no nonzero setpoint is sent
Arm does not replay a direction
  • GIVEN previous motion intent exists
  • WHEN R is pressed and ARM succeeds
  • THEN the client starts armed at zero and requires a subsequent motion key

Gentle planar directions

W/S SHALL request forward/backward, A/D left/right strafe, and Q/E counter-clockwise/clockwise rotation in base_link. Only one direction SHALL be active at a time. Translation magnitude SHALL be min(0.1 m/s, the advertised axis maximum), rotation min(0.3 rad/s, advertised maximum). Disabled axes SHALL remain zero. Other Twist components SHALL be zero; simultaneous keys SHALL not combine velocities.

Limits below the defaults are respected
  • GIVEN an armed client whose advertised max_vx is 0.05 m/s
  • WHEN W is received
  • THEN vx is 0.05 and vy/wz are zero
New direction replaces the previous one
  • GIVEN W was the current direction
  • WHEN E is received
  • THEN vx/vy become zero and only clockwise wz is requested

Input expiry and latest intent

Each recognized motion key SHALL expire 250 ms after its monotonic receipt time. The next send after expiry SHALL be zero. Key repeats SHALL refresh that window; unrelated keys SHALL not. Buffered motion SHALL not form a playback queue. STOP, quit, disarm and failure SHALL clear buffered motion. The client SHALL describe key repeat as renewal, not claim it receives physical key-release events.

Motion input expires
  • GIVEN W was received at t and no subsequent motion key arrives
  • WHEN a send occurs at or after t+250 ms
  • THEN the transmitted setpoint is zero
Stop wins over buffered movement
  • WHEN a read batch contains movement and Space or quit
  • THEN movement is discarded and no later queued key replays it

Periodic stream and scheduling failure

While connected, the client SHALL send the current zero or armed intent every 50 ms with wrapping u32 setpoint sequences. It SHALL process received stops and input expiry before each send. A send-loop gap of at least 200 ms SHALL clear intent and end the run through cleanup; catching up SHALL not send a backlog of motion. Host scheduling SHALL not be described as a guaranteed physical stopping bound.

Delayed loop cannot replay motion
  • GIVEN nonzero intent and a 200 ms gap since the last send-loop iteration
  • WHEN the client resumes
  • THEN it sends no further nonzero setpoint and enters cleanup

Validate and correlate device input

The client SHALL accept only correctly framed/versioned replies from the selected endpoint, validating payload lengths and codes. After claim, Status SHALL match the current session and either a pending control sequence or the unsolicited sequence zero. Wrong-peer, malformed, stale-session and unmatched replies SHALL not authorize motion or extend reply deadlines. Unsolicited stopped Status SHALL disable local motion before the next send.

Queued notification precedes an ARM reply
  • WHEN a stopped notification arrives before the matching ARM reply
  • THEN the client clears motion and does not confuse the notification with a successful ARM
Intruder packet cannot enable movement
  • WHEN another endpoint or session sends an Armed Status
  • THEN local arming remains unchanged

Link checks without automatic recovery

The client SHALL check link responsiveness using nonce/sequence-matched Echo every 250 ms, allowing 500 ms for each reply. Echo SHALL not be described as proof of ownership or arming. A missed Echo/control deadline, socket error or terminal loss SHALL clear intent and terminate through cleanup. The client SHALL send no HELLO after its initial handshake and SHALL never reconnect or re-arm automatically.

Lost link requires a new operator session
  • WHEN an Echo or ARM reply deadline expires
  • THEN local motion stops, cleanup runs, and no automatic HELLO or ARM is sent

Bounded shutdown and honest reporting

Space SHALL clear motion and request STOP; quit, Ctrl-C, EOF and handled errors SHALL also exit through cleanup. Cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP and BYE within 500 ms total without indefinite waits, even if an earlier send fails, and restore terminal settings. Successful STOP acknowledgement SHALL require matching stopped/Stop Status. The client SHALL label unacknowledged stops and BYE as unconfirmed attempts, never verified wheel stop or release.

Cleanup tolerates a failed send
  • WHEN sending zero or STOP fails during cleanup
  • THEN BYE and terminal restoration are still attempted within the cleanup deadline

Observable commands and evidence limits

The client SHALL show connection/local-arm state, session, last valid device Status, reply age and requested vx/vy/wz. Last-reported Status SHALL be distinguished from live physical state; Echo SHALL not refresh Status age. Documentation SHALL identify open-loop speeds as approximate and UDP cleanup as best effort. Simulator passes SHALL not count as wheel, radio or electrical acceptance.

A responsive rebooted device does not prove ownership
  • GIVEN the car reboots and answers Echo but does not accept the old session
  • WHEN the client displays its state
  • THEN it shows Status as last reported with its original age, sends no new HELLO and does not claim ownership recovery

openspec/specs/motor-control/spec.md

motor control

motor-control Specification

Purpose

Controls four motor channels independently with explicit enable, standby, duty mapping and fault behavior, without depending on device kinematics or transports.

Requirements

Four independent wheel commands

Motor control SHALL accept four signed wheel commands in −1.0..=1.0, ordered FL, FR, RR, RL. Positive means forward for that wheel. Magnitude SHALL be converted by the documented deadband/duty rule, not assumed proportional to physical speed. Each command SHALL affect its own wheel only, with no kinematic mixing.

Each wheel is driven on its own
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (0.5, 0, 0, 0)
  • THEN only FL is driven forward at the duty produced by the deadband/duty rule
  • AND FR, RR and RL receive a zero wheel command
Sign sets direction
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (−0.5, −0.5, −0.5, −0.5)
  • THEN every wheel turns in the direction that moves the car backward

Independent of transport and kinematics

Motor control SHALL expose configuration, wheel commands, enable/standby and typed validation faults. It SHALL NOT depend on setpoints, mecanum kinematics, the source or the session.

Built without the device layer
  • GIVEN the motor control module
  • WHEN it is compiled and host-tested on its own
  • THEN it builds without the setpoint, kinematics, arbiter or transport modules

Invalid wheel commands stop the wheels

Motor control SHALL clamp a finite wheel command outside −1.0..=1.0 to the nearest bound. A non-finite wheel command (NaN or infinity) SHALL put every driver in standby and report a fault, even when the other three are valid.

Out-of-range value is clamped
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (1.5, 0, 0, 0)
  • THEN FL is driven as for 1.0
NaN stops every wheel
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled and all four wheels are driven
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (NaN, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
  • THEN every driver is put in standby
  • AND a fault is reported

Standby until explicitly enabled

Every motor driver SHALL be in standby from power-up, through reset and firmware recovery, until motor control is explicitly enabled. Disabling motor control SHALL put every driver in standby.

Boot does not move a wheel
  • GIVEN the car is powered off with motors connected
  • WHEN it powers up, resets, or recovers from a reset
  • THEN every driver's STBY input stays inactive until motor control is enabled
  • AND no wheel turns

Standby on safety stop

When the device raises a safety stop, the coordinator SHALL request standby in the control tick that processes the stop, and motor control SHALL set every wheel command to zero and deassert both STBY outputs before any further bridge update. A measured pin-level bound is deferred (O4: needs a logic analyzer or oscilloscope); this change SHALL NOT claim one.

Watchdog timeout puts every driver in standby
  • GIVEN the car is armed and all four wheels are driven
  • WHEN a watchdog timeout raises a safety stop
  • THEN both STBY outputs are deasserted in that control tick, before any further bridge update
  • AND on the bench every wheel stops

Full-scale maps to the configured limit

Wheel command 1.0 SHALL map to the configured maximum PWM duty, enforced independently for each wheel. The car SHALL use open-loop duty control without encoder feedback. The product profile SHALL cap drive duty at 70%, the envelope M4 verified (O1). Raising the cap SHALL require new qualification. Duty limiting SHALL NOT be advertised as current protection; start and stall current are not measured.

Product profile full scale
  • GIVEN the product profile: deadband 0.02, minimum duty 40%, maximum duty 70%
  • WHEN a wheel receives 1.0, then 0.5, then 1.5
  • THEN the requested duties are 70%, 55% and 70%
  • AND no command drives any wheel above 70%

Zero command behaviour

A zero wheel command SHALL request coast for that wheel without disabling a driven neighbour on the same driver. On the TB6612, this SHALL use IN1=IN2=low and PWM=high while STBY is high. A safety stop SHALL instead deassert both drivers' STBY inputs. Coast distance is not measured or claimed (O5). Source: Toshiba H-SW table, page 4.

Zero coasts a turning wheel
  • GIVEN a wheel driven at 0.5
  • WHEN it receives a zero wheel command
  • THEN its outputs are high impedance and it is allowed to coast
A zero wheel does not disable its neighbour
  • GIVEN FL and RL share driver 1 and motor control is enabled
  • WHEN FL receives zero and RL receives 0.5
  • THEN FL requests coast with both direction pins low and PWM high
  • AND RL retains its requested duty and driver 1 remains enabled

Dead zone handling

Exact zero or a magnitude below the configured deadband SHALL request coast. Otherwise duty SHALL be min + abs(command) * (max - min), rounded to permille after input clamping. The initial deadband SHALL be 0.02 and minimum duty 40%; maximum duty SHALL be configured. A precision minimum physical speed SHALL NOT be inferred from this rule. The stand starting observation was about 35%, not a universal per-wheel threshold.

Small command behaviour is predictable
  • GIVEN deadband 0.02, minimum duty 40% and maximum duty 100%
  • WHEN the wheel receives 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.5 and 1.0 in turn
  • THEN the requested modes/duties are coast, coast, 41.2%, 70% and 100%
  • AND negative commands use the same duty magnitude with reversed direction

Starts and reversals do not reset the controller

Motor control SHALL support direct signed changes, without a slew limit, up to the product cap. M4 reversed all four wheels between ±70% ten times without an ESP32 reset or BLE loss (O7). Operation above 70% SHALL NOT be claimed without new qualification.

Full reversal on all wheels
  • GIVEN the product profile (maximum 70%) and all four wheels at 1.0
  • WHEN all four are commanded to −1.0 in one control tick
  • THEN the ESP32-S3 does not reset and the owner's session survives

Calibrated wheel mapping

Motor control SHALL configure each wheel's driver channel and inversion. The current car mapping SHALL be D1 A→FL, D1 B→RL, D2 A→FR, D2 B→RR, with all inversions false because directions were corrected at connectors. Both separate STBY outputs SHALL follow motor enable/disable together.

Positive command moves each wheel forward
  • GIVEN the car restrained with wheels clear
  • WHEN each wheel in turn receives 0.3 alone
  • THEN the wheel at that position turns, in the direction that moves the car forward

Configuration validation

Before enabling, motor control SHALL validate finite deadband in [0,1), integer duty limits 0 ≤ min ≤ max ≤ 1000 permille, and a one-to-one mapping of four wheels to four bridge channels. Invalid configuration SHALL report a configuration fault and keep both drivers disabled. Configuration SHALL be immutable while enabled; replacing it SHALL disable and clear stored commands before validation.

Invalid duty or mapping cannot enable
  • GIVEN minimum duty 800 and maximum 700, or two wheels assigned to the same channel
  • WHEN configuration is installed and enable requested
  • THEN configuration is rejected and both STBY signals stay low
Invalid floating-point configuration cannot drive
  • GIVEN deadband NaN, infinity, negative or at least 1
  • WHEN configuration is installed
  • THEN a configuration fault is reported before any driver enable

Fault recovery requires explicit enable

A non-finite wheel vector SHALL invalidate stored commands and latch motor control disabled. Subsequent wheel updates SHALL NOT clear the latch. Explicit enable with a valid configuration and a complete finite wheel vector SHALL be required to recover; enabling SHALL NOT replay a previously stored vector. Standby SHALL always work, including in a fault state.

Valid updates do not clear a fault
  • GIVEN a NaN command caused both drivers to enter standby
  • WHEN several finite wheel updates arrive without explicit enable
  • THEN both drivers remain disabled
  • AND a later explicit enable with a new finite vector clears the command fault and applies only that vector

Complete vector validation before output

Motor control SHALL validate the entire vector before applying any channel, so a bad fourth value cannot partially drive the first three. Standby SHALL deassert both STBY outputs before preparing any new direction/PWM state. On enable, valid bridge states SHALL be prepared while disabled before STBY is asserted. Driver faults SHALL be reported to the caller, not silently converted to successful commands.

Fourth invalid wheel cannot cause partial motion
  • GIVEN drivers are disabled and a recording host driver
  • WHEN enable receives (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, infinity)
  • THEN no enable-high or drive update is issued for any bridge
Safe enable ordering
  • GIVEN disabled motor control with a valid configuration
  • WHEN it is explicitly enabled with a finite vector
  • THEN both drivers remain disabled until all four bridge states are prepared

Coast is independent of the drive duty cap

The configured maximum SHALL limit driven PWM duty, not the PWM-high signal required by the documented coast mode. A coast request SHALL keep both direction inputs low while PWM is high; it SHALL NOT become forward drive or brake merely because the configured drive cap is below 100%.

Coast with a reduced maximum
  • GIVEN maximum drive duty 70%, FL at zero and RL at 1.0
  • WHEN their shared driver is enabled
  • THEN FL has both direction pins low and PWM high, while RL is driven at 70%

openspec/changes/add-iphone-ble-client/design.md

iPhone BLE web controller design (draft)

Context

See proposal for the selected scope and acceptance gate. The accepted car API remains unchanged. The laptop client supplies the gentle-direction/explicit-arm precedent; UDP handshake/correlation does not apply to BLE. Q9/Q18/Q19/Q21 remain the roadmap's home.

Recorded user decisions (2026-10-20)

  • Linux only; no Mac or paid Apple Developer membership; avoid a subscription.
  • Target a web controller opened in Bluefy on iPhone.
  • Phone supports the 72-byte payload (Todor's confirmation, not a new measured app/board result).
  • Six press-and-hold buttons first; allow a later accelerometer-based input without changing the device API or bypassing safety policy. Todor then explicitly accepted the revised proposal for button implementation; see acceptance record.

Existing protocol evidence

Inspected at main 1be50b3; no protocol change is proposed.

Concern Existing evidence and client consequence
Advertisement/claim Firmware BLE loop: flags and Rovi M8 in scan response, no service UUID. Use a name filter plus optional service access, then validate GATT. Connecting claims immediately and switches off the AP. Name/device ID is not authentication.
GATT RoviService: service d47a0010-45b2-4d19-8db0-6bd87e9c0001; same suffix with 0011 Setpoint (write without response), 0012 Control (write with response), 0013 Capabilities (read), 0014 Status (read/notify), 0015 Echo (write without response/notify). Require the first four characteristics/properties; Echo is unused.
Setpoint Python wire reference and Rust decoder: u32 LE sequence + 68-byte little-endian TwistStamped CDR = 72 bytes. Empty frame means base_link; zero timestamp is valid; only vx/vy/wz vary. No UDP header, BLE numeric session, HELLO or BYE.
Capabilities Encoder: u8 version, five f32 LE (radius, centre projection sum, max_vx/max_vy/max_wz), three u16 LE (lease/claim/reclaim ms), 27 bytes. Widen f32 values exactly; never round limits upward.
Status/control Encoder: states 0 Open/1 Claimed/2 Armed/3 Stopped; reasons 0 none/1 Stop/2 LeaseExpired/3 OwnerLost/4 OutOfLimits; errors 0 none/1 Busy/2 NotOwner/3 NotReady/4 Invalid. Require reason=0 except Stopped, whose reason must be nonzero. ARM=1/STOP=2; refused writes use ATT Value Not Allowed.
Windows Defaults: lease 1000, claim 10000, reclaim 5000 ms. Read advertised values. Disarmed zero setpoints retain ownership; STOP retains it; disconnect releases it. Firmware disconnects on ownership expiry.
Prior evidence Bleak client, product Status/Echo probe and BLE lease results inform the wire contract, not Bluefy performance.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goals: Linux-authorable static controller, one foreground phone session, button-first operation, testable codecs/session policy and separate browser/radio/wheel evidence.

Non-Goals: native app/scaffold/signing, sensor driving in v1, firmware/security changes, station mode, background driving, automatic recovery, calibration or measured speed. No hosted site is published by this change until task 3.2.

Decisions

Bluefy web delivery from Linux

Use static HTML/CSS/JavaScript under apps/iphone/ with no third-party runtime scripts. Load a versioned page over HTTPS in Bluefy. No command backend, account or paid developer membership is needed for our web code. Propose a repository GitHub Pages deployment at https://tptodorov.github.io/rovi/iphone/ (not a live URL claimed by this draft). GitHub Pages supports static sites in public repositories on GitHub Free. Prepare only the app assets, preserving any existing site configuration; confirm the final origin/HTTPS during delivery. The page is trusted controller code: no third-party runtime scripts or secrets. This spec PR performs no deployment.

Why this route: Apple's Xcode requirements require macOS; free Personal Team provisioning uses Xcode and expires after seven days. A remote Mac can compile a native app, but compilation alone does not solve free signing/install from this Linux setup. Bluefy's developer guide documents HTTPS-page BLE control; its App Store listing lists it as free. This replaces the earlier SwiftUI/CoreBluetooth proposal rather than adding a second client.

Bluefy is a required installed host, not proof that every Web Bluetooth function or inactive-state signal works on the selected phone. Feature checks and P1/P3 must fail closed where support is absent. Safari/Home Screen web apps are not promised substitutes; WebKit's tracking issue records the Web Bluetooth limitation. No Expo/React Native wrapper is needed.

Selection and setup

The page's Choose & Connect action explains the ownership/AP effect, then invokes requestDevice with filters: [{name: 'Rovi M8'}] and optionalServices: [serviceUUID]. Selecting in the browser picker is the explicit target choice; only then connect while the page is active. Picker presentation/dismissal is browser-controlled: do not promise a custom scan list, RSSI, hardware addresses, a cancellable scan API or a ten-second picker timeout. Same-name candidates are not authenticated identities; display the selected name and opaque browser ID when available.

Start the ten-second setup deadline at GATT connect invocation after selection, not while the person considers the picker. Discover/validate required properties, exact capabilities, valid Claimed/Stopped Status and notifications; submit an initial 72-byte zero setpoint without response, with no ARM. Claim starts before discovery completes; a firmware timeout fails setup without automatic reconnect. Reject lease<500 ms, claim<1000 ms or invalid/nonpositive windows/geometry. Current defaults exceed these supported-profile floors; these are proposed client bounds, not iOS measurements.

The phone payload capability is user-confirmed. Web Bluetooth does not expose CoreBluetooth's MTU/write-capacity/readiness APIs. Show packet size 72 and MTU/capacity as unavailable unless actually measured externally. A rejected initial zero submission is incompatibility; promise resolution is not proof of firmware receipt. An explicit later zero+ARM/Status transaction and P1 establish the browser/firmware path. Never fragment or switch protocols automatically.

Button input with a later sensor option

Separate the input interpreter from the session/transmitter: buttons produce only latest planar intent and its expiry; one shared policy owns arming, caps, STOP, lifecycle and connection generations. No generic plugin framework or unused sensor implementation is needed. A future accelerometer/tilt interpreter would feed that same intent boundary; it cannot arm or write GATT directly. It needs a separate reviewed proposal for axis mapping, calibration, dead zone, enable/deadman gesture, permission refusal, sensor loss and input switching. The motion/orientation standard defines sensor APIs, not a guarantee that Bluefy exposes them. V1 does not request motion permission or consume sensor data.

The v1 page has Choose & Connect, local/reported state, ARM, prominent STOP, six labelled hold buttons, requested values and Disconnect. Buttons use pointer tracking/capture with explicit bounds checks; pointerup/cancel, lost capture, leaving bounds or another direction invalidates the hold. Renew the held input only from active visible UI animation frames, never the transmit timer; a stalled UI expires after 250 ms even if BLE work continues. Re-entry requires a new press. Text/accessibility labels, large targets, text sizing and cues beyond color apply; accessibility activation never creates a sticky nonzero toggle. Actual hold accessibility/usability remains a P3 acceptance check.

Stream, controls and Status

One session generation and operation epoch own all asynchronous work. Serialize GATT procedures; keep at most one pending setpoint write promise and one coalesced latest intent, never a motion queue. Every 50 ms, check lifecycle, stops and input expiry before choosing a sample. Do not start another write while the prior procedure is pending. A scheduler/submission gap>=200 ms fails the run; do not catch up. A write-without-response promise is host progress, not an acknowledgement of applied motion. Fair scheduling must leave space for Status/control within these bounds; P2 measures the complete workload.

ARM invalidates touches, submits fresh zero, then performs one writeValueWithResponse ARM. Only its successful current-generation promise plus the subsequently requested readValue result Armed/none/none grants local motion permission; one second covers the whole action. Copy the returned bytes immediately. Notifications never grant arm. Unlike native delegate callbacks, Web Bluetooth provides an explicit read promise; there is no need to repeatedly disable notifications to identify read results. Ignore stale promise completions and never use cached characteristic.value to confirm controls.

STOP immediately invalidates pending local ARM and all holds, takes scheduling priority, and requires successful Control=2 write plus a subsequent read Stopped/Stop/none within one second. An in-flight GATT procedure cannot be assumed cancellable; keep intent zero, attempt STOP when possible, and disconnect on timeout. Confirmed STOP retains zero streaming/ownership; only a new explicit ARM and new press can resume. Notifications can revoke permission; repeated reports of the same stopped state while recovering do not create a new stop, but a new stop transition during ARM invalidates it.

Schedule an explicit Status read every 500 ms, at most one pending transaction; a control confirmation read also counts. A transaction lasting>=1000 ms, malformed result, GATT error, Open or unexpected Armed ends the run. Status notifications/reads do not renew the firmware lease. Treat disconnection events and observed service/permission loss as failure. Web APIs need not expose native powered-off/resetting/permission distinctions: use specific errors when known and honest unavailable/disconnected wording otherwise.

Lifecycle and bounded shutdown

During setup/connection, use page visibility, blur, pagehide/navigation and any verified Bluefy host inactivity signal to clear holds and end the session. Before GATT connection, a browser picker can itself change focus; that focus change cannot drive anything. Recheck page activity after selection and never connect from an inactive page or a cancelled attempt. Gate every send on the current active/visible state; foreground return, page reload or a remembered device grant cannot reconnect or re-arm automatically. Do not opt into Bluefy background peripheral access or prevent screen locking. Browser/native lifecycle events are not interchangeable: P3 must verify actual lock, app switch, browser UI and interruption behavior; if an undetected inactive state allows renewed nonzero submissions, this browser/version is unsupported for driving.

Disconnect/failure first clears intent and stops the normal stream. Under one 500 ms deadline while runnable, independently attempt zero and STOP where possible, then invoke local gatt.disconnect() even if a promise fails/hangs. Cancel generations and ignore late completions; a connect promise resolving after shutdown is disconnected again. A browser picker cannot be forcibly dismissed by an invented API; a late selection never connects after its local attempt was cancelled.

Suspension/termination may prevent any cleanup. Firmware lease/window handling remains the independent fallback; local disconnect or resolved writes do not establish physical link teardown, ownership release or wheel stop. Show requested, device-reported and unconfirmed states separately, retaining the original Status observation age.

Platform sources checked 2026-10-20

Web Bluetooth specification defines secure-context user selection, service access, characteristic properties, separate write modes, read promises and notification events. These are API contracts, not evidence that Bluefy implements every method. Bluefy's official site and guide document its GATT bridge and HTTPS requirement. The App Store release notes mention a host app-state hook; exact hook registration/semantics must be verified instead of guessed. Apple's foreground/background guide explains why suspension cannot be treated as a runnable cleanup opportunity.

OPEN questions and acceptance gates

Item How to settle Blocks
I1 — browser/environment and delivery checks Record iPhone model/iOS/Bluefy version. Confirm split write methods, read/notify, name-only picker and lifecycle signals. Verify the proposed GitHub Pages origin/HTTPS during delivery, preserving existing site configuration; publication remains a future authorized task. Linux-only/no-membership, Bluefy and the proposed free hosting route are recorded choices. Deployment and phone acceptance; independent Linux codec/UI/session work can proceed after task 1.1.
I2 — browser payload integration, phone capability confirmed Todor confirms phone 72-byte support. P1 checks the actual Bluefy path with zero+explicit ARM/Status at zero; keep runtime rejection handling. Record measured ATT MTU only if instrumentation provides it; do not fabricate capacity from Web Bluetooth or mark new board evidence passed. Browser compatibility acceptance, not a repeated question about whether the phone supports 72 bytes.
I3 — Q19 full workload P2 measures 60 s at 20 Hz with Status reads and zero ARM/STOP: no lease expiry, >=200 ms submission gap or one-second control/read timeout. Record connection interval only if measured. Failure requires reviewed changes, not silently relaxed bounds. Phone acceptance and motor batch; BlueZ results do not pass it.
I4 — lifecycle/accessibility verification Button-first interaction is selected. P3 verifies actual touch, text/accessibility, blur/hidden/lock/interruption behavior and no background renewal of motion. Missing host signals must still produce expiry/lease fallback; persistent hidden motion fails support. UI/phone acceptance, not the selected button layout.

Button implementation is authorized by the acceptance record; physical/product acceptance remains pending. Unmeasured browser/hardware results cannot count as passed acceptance; see verification.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Browser dependency and opaque picker/state APIs → feature gates and actual-phone checks; no native feature assumptions or guessed host hooks.
  • Browser scheduling/buffered writes and suspension → expiring UI intent, bounded application work and firmware lease fallback. Proposed software deadlines are not physical stopping bounds.
  • Public static controller code and same-name peers → controlled HTTPS origin, no remote runtime scripts, explicit selection and GATT validation; these do not add authenticated identity to the existing API.
  • Zero streaming deliberately retains ownership after STOP → visible ownership effect and Disconnect. Open-loop gentle references can overcome motor deadband; they are not measured physical speeds.

Migration Plan

After explicit acceptance, implement/test the static page from Linux, prepare a reviewable HTTPS deployment, and publish only within an authorized delivery task. Then run separately authorized phone checks and a separately announced supervised wheels-off-ground batch. Rollback is disconnecting/closing the page and withdrawing its deployment; no firmware migration. Archive after product acceptance, never after this planning PR alone.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/design.md

M6 implementation design

Context

See proposal for scope and evidence. M8 has a host-tested no_std core plus separate firmware and simulator packages; M4 added a pure motor mapping function that currently imports the arbiter state. The working firmware remains our bench reference. This change extracts that behavior and applies the reviewed corrections, with no automatic flash or measurement sweep.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goal: independent motor control, one device contract for all transports, explicit validation/fault boundaries and repeatable conformance tests. Non-goals: a new HAL framework, closed-loop velocity control, runtime tuning UI or new physical qualification claims. The current geometry and accepted M5 references remain the inputs; no gain fitting is planned.

Decisions

Package boundaries

Cargo.toml                      workspace: reusable no_std crates only
crates/rovi-core/                codecs, arbiter, geometry, graph, device
crates/rovi-motor-control/       configuration, mapping, enable/fault state
crates/rovi-drive/               coordinator: device state → motor control, fault → device stop
apps/simcar/                    separate workspace/lockfile; host adapters
firmware/                      separate workspace/lockfile; ESP32 adapters
experiments/                   retained standalone bench reference

Exclude apps/simcar, firmware and the existing experimental packages from the root workspace. M8 separated host ROS dependencies and ESP dependencies because their crypto dependency resolutions conflicted; M6 will preserve that separation rather than solve unrelated dependency upgrades. Product applications depend on the reusable crates by path. Keep the pinned zenoh fork and current target/toolchain settings initially.

Copy the working core and tests into the product crates, preserving source history through the extraction commit. Experiments stay independently buildable and frozen as evidence; subsequent product fixes live in the product crates. This bounded duplication preserves rollback and avoids silently changing the firmware used to obtain old results. After product acceptance, archive the experiments as references rather than maintaining two active implementations.

rovi-core returns normalized wheel demands and state effects. It does not import the motor driver or HAL. rovi-motor-control has no dependency on the arbiter, kinematics or transports. The coordinator, rovi-drive (2026-10-17), connects them; it depends on both, so the integration and fault-injection tests run on the laptop, which a coordinator inside the ESP32-only firmware would not allow. A small output boundary (rovi_motor_control::Driver: STBY per driver, pins per bridge) exposes standby and bridge updates to the ESP implementation or a recording test double; no generic robotics framework is needed. All three crates build without std.

Drive::new(motor, &mut Device) binds before transport startup. Invalid motor configuration inhibits explicit ARM with not-ready and prevents ROS auto-arm before the first tick; the core only sees readiness, with no dependency on the motor crate. The firmware logs invalid boot motor configuration as motor_config. The simulator defaults to ready without a physical driver.

Drive::tick(&mut Device, now) runs every control tick: the device's timers first, then the motors. A change of the arbiter's arm_count is the only enable operation, so a STOP and re-ARM between two ticks still drops STBY first; while armed it updates the bridges, otherwise it puts both drivers in standby. It returns the device Effects and the tick's motor fault as an events::Fault (ev=error src=motor_*); Drive::motor().fault() gives the typed detail.

Configuration and fault boundary

Validate immutable device and motor profiles before accepting control. Canonicalize advertised floating values through f32 and use those values for limit comparisons, so a limit read over BLE is actually accepted. Geometry normalization remains 40 rad/s and reference limits 1/1/3 in the named experimental profile, not measured physical maxima. The product motor profile is minimum duty 40%, deadband 0.02 and maximum 70% (O1); the experiment firmware keeps its 100% cap as the comparison reference. No profile is labelled production-qualified merely because it compiles.

Motor operations are explicit enable with a complete vector, update while enabled, and standby. Validate the full vector before any drive output. A bad vector disables and latches the motor layer; ordinary updates cannot clear it. Prepare all bridge states while standby is inactive before enabling. Preserve 20 kHz PWM and the separate standby pins. Coast uses the datasheet pin state even when the drive duty cap is less than 100%.

On a motor validation failure, the coordinator immediately requests device out-of-limits stop, records the typed internal fault, and keeps both drivers disabled. This reuses existing status codes rather than introducing an incompatible reason enum. Only a fresh accepted setpoint followed by explicit ARM can call motor enable again; checking state == Armed on every tick is not an enable operation. Invalid motor configuration cannot be recovered through remote ARM; replace the configuration while disabled or reboot with a valid build. Invalid device configuration fails control initialization entirely.

Input processing and ownership

Process due deadlines before input; then validate envelope/identity, payload, ordering and limits before committing state. An initial ROS claim requires a known publisher and a finite, planar, supported-frame, in-limits setpoint. Out-of-limits input from an existing owner raises a stop; malformed, stale or non-owner input does not mutate the lease or sequence history.

Use wrapping u32 ordering for BLE/UDP. ROS keeps full i64 counters per publisher GID, including separate arm and setpoint streams; compare only within the same stream, then order valid samples from different owner publishers by receipt. Keep bounded graph identity and session ordering tables (16 entries each initially). Graph removal invalidates identity, but retain all accepted owner GID high-water marks until session release; unrelated graph churn cannot reset replay checks. Drop input from additional owner publishers if no ordering slot remains. Unknown publishers cannot drive until announced again. A live publisher must not reset its sequence under an unchanged GID; it must create a new publisher. ROS sequence values are not narrowed to u32.

UDP session allocation uses a boot-randomized nonzero u32 seed and increments per new claim, skipping zero; a current owner's repeated HELLO is idempotent. BLE callbacks carry a local connection generation to distinguish reused handles. Clear queued inputs on release and adapter reconnect. ROS has no Rovi session ID in its payload: these measures isolate local queues and known publisher lifetimes, but do not promise authenticated replay prevention across router/client restarts. Security remains the trusted local-link baseline in ADR-0008.

BLE disconnect and UDP BYE release their owning session. A detected ROS router disconnect does the same; publisher silence or missing liveliness triggers the independent lease path when fresh setpoints cease. Reconnect rebuilds graph state and declarations before samples can claim again. Wi-Fi stays up for both UDP and ROS; the arbiter performs their mutual exclusion.

ROS capabilities and status

Use shared typed capabilities/status snapshots; adapters serialize the same values. Preserve existing BLE/UDP frame layouts and numeric status codes. Implement persistent last-control-error state for every transport, not only BLE. BLE refreshes its readable value synchronously with changes; UDP sends its existing STATUS frame on owner control replies and stop transitions. Release leaves the externally readable state open; owner-lost is also recorded as a stop event, not a persistent stopped state with no owner.

ROS uses bounded CDR strings and the exact key/units contract in the spec. Both ROS adapters compare the shared Status snapshot every 10 ms and publish observed changes plus a 900 ms heartbeat; reconnect resets the publication schedule. session=0 denotes no owner. BLE refreshes the GATT value before reads and after control/setpoint writes, then notifies changes. UDP adapters poll for pending owner stop notifications even without incoming datagrams; unsolicited STATUS uses sequence 0, direct replies echo the request sequence. No measured velocity field is added.

O9 closed on 2026-10-17: the pinned ordinary publisher did not serve retained history to a late Jazzy transient-local subscriber; the same subscriber received its later live sample (evidence). Use the approved reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback. capabilities::Publication publishes every 900 ms (headroom under one second) and on observed session/owner changes; each new router connection starts a fresh schedule. Both adapters poll it every 10 ms and serialize Device::capabilities_snapshot() through the same bounded CDR encoder. Controllers subscribe with volatile durability. Transport disconnection can delay delivery; publication schedules are not guarantees during packet loss or an unavailable router.

Compatibility changes to verify

Compared with M8, intentionally correct per-wheel coast, validate configuration, latch internal motor faults, support u32 rollover and full ROS per-publisher ordering, reject unsupported frames, and process deadlines before commands. Preserve ROS auto-arm only for claim/lease-expiry and explicit ARM after STOP/out-of-limits. Add the already-agreed ROS capabilities/status content and consistent owner error persistence. These are contract improvements, not claims that extraction is behavior-identical. Client golden vectors retain version 1 layouts; existing client tools remain the bench interface.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Coast differs from the experiment's all-low output: reproduce the pin mismatch in a failing host test first; product physical stopping remains unqualified until bench acceptance.
  • Lower-layer fault accidentally re-enables on the next tick: integration tests inject faults through the coordinator and exercise continued ROS streaming, explicit recovery and session release.
  • Independent ROS publishers cannot share a sequence counter: per-GID histories plus same-node authorization; test duplicate, out-of-order and interleaved publishers.
  • Extraction breaks the target build or Python tools: keep separate app lockfiles, run existing socket/ROS scenarios against the product sim and cross-build both firmware features.
  • Known measurements are narrow: carry their evidence labels; do not replace normalization or claim electrical/stopping maxima from short pulses.

Migration and acceptance

Implement in the order in tasks: baseline extraction, motor seam, device conformance, ROS observability, then qualified firmware acceptance. Tests accompany each behavioral correction. Add product checks alongside existing experiment CI while the old firmware remains the rollback reference; update client/runbook executable paths when the product sim and firmware exist.

The scenario-to-test index is created before implementation and completed with actual test names/results as each task lands. Host-only scenarios stay host-only; radio, physical output, timing and thermal claims require their corresponding bench evidence. No motor run or flash is implicit in proposal acceptance.

Deferred qualification

O1, O2, O5 and O7 are decided (2026-10-17): 70% product cap, measured geometry with approximate references, coast for a zero wheel, direct reversals within the cap. This change does not claim what was not measured:

Not claimed Needs
Start and stall current (O1) A current monitor (INA226) or an oscilloscope with a shunt
Numeric STBY disable bound (O4) A logic analyzer or oscilloscope
Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband and coast with a driven neighbour (task 5.2, skipped by Todor 2026-10-19) A multimeter/logic probe for static levels; timing/PWM-capable tools for duty/deadband checks
Operation above 70% (O1, O7) Requalification with the equipment above
Coast distance and maximum speeds (O5, O2) Tape and video; not scheduled

They return as a new change when a requirement needs them. O9 is the laptop capability test with the fixed fallback above. No new measurement sweep is scheduled.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-laptop-teleoperation/design.md

Laptop teleoperation design

Context

See the proposal for motivation and accepted laptop scope. The existing car API and M6 evidence are the boundaries. apps/simcar/scenarios/wire.py already supplies golden-tested TwistStamped, Status and capability codecs; its scenario Client is a test helper, not a product transport.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goal: one small Linux terminal client whose policy can be tested with injected time and socket/terminal boundaries. Non-goals: a client framework, configurable bindings/speeds, multi-axis mixing, runtime firmware changes, station networking or proof of physical velocity/stopping distance.

Decisions

  • Use Python’s standard library (socket, select, terminal facilities, monotonic time), invoked from the repository as python3 -m apps.teleop --target HOST:PORT. No new runtime dependency or global installation. A browser UI or gamepad adds another input/runtime boundary without being needed for this first interface.
  • Keep policy separate from terminal/socket effects: a current intent, expiry, local arm gate and pending request deadlines. A single event loop handles input/replies before a 50 ms stream tick; no thread or command queue. Reject leases below 200 ms rather than promise a faster supported host cadence. A 200 ms scheduling gap fails closed; this is host policy, not a measured wheel-stop bound.
  • Use R for arm, WASD translation, QE rotation, Space STOP, Esc/Ctrl-C quit. Terminal bytes provide key repeats, not trustworthy key-up/focus events: each direction is a 250 ms request that needs renewal. Drain buffered input to the latest motion intent; stop/quit overrides that batch, and arming clears it. Never replay accumulated input after a scheduling gap. Zero intent keeps the owner’s lease live while idle/disarmed; Space sends STOP while retaining the session and zero stream.
  • Share, rather than copy, the existing payload codec in a small apps/client Python package. Keep a thin compatibility import at the existing scenario module path so bench/ROS/experimental users retain their imports and golden tests. Add frame validation in the client boundary; avoid converting every existing test helper into a production client in the same change.
  • Correlate every control reply by endpoint, session and a nonzero request sequence; preserve unsolicited sequence-zero stops separately. Use wrapping u32 setpoint ordering independently. Only one ARM may be pending. If a stopped notification arrives while ARM is pending, cancel that request locally; a delayed Armed reply cannot revive local motion. A later R sends zero and a new request. Do not retry ARM automatically.
  • Echo checks only reachability. UDP has no observational owner-status read, and HELLO can claim after a reset. Therefore perform HELLO only once and label Status as last reported with its own age. A reset may leave a responsive car rejecting the old session; this client never claims it silently. A new operator-started process is required to reclaim after terminal/link failure.
  • All connect/control waits and cleanup are bounded. On exit try zero, STOP, BYE; catch individual send failures so later cleanup still runs, then restore terminal state in an outer finally block. STOP success needs the matching state/reason acknowledgement; BYE has no release acknowledgement and remains best effort. No promise that the wheel stopped merely because a datagram was sent.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Terminal repeat may begin after the 250 ms window, producing an initial pause → document this pulse/renewal behavior; deterministic expiry matters more than pretending key-up exists.
  • Wi-Fi can silently stall (#23) → missed Echo deadlines end the client, the device lease remains independent, and no reconnect is automatic. This change does not diagnose or close #23.
  • UDP can lose a stop or release → bounded best effort and explicit unconfirmed reporting; retain the device watchdog. No application-level emergency-stop guarantee.
  • Existing source/net and motor bench evidence does not qualify a new terminal application → simulator/PTY evidence first, then a separately announced gentle stand batch; no loaded/floor test or electrical measurement is implied.

Migration and rollback

Add the client without firmware or API changes. Preserve the current codec import through a compatibility module and rerun its existing tests and simulator scenarios. Keep the normal ROS firmware installed. Rollback removes the new application and restores the codec location; no board image or protocol migration is needed.

Scope decision

Todor selected the laptop client on 2026-10-20 after reviewing the concrete option in #89. Implementation uses the proposed keys, 250 ms intent window and gentle defaults; no new ADR is needed for these reversible client choices.

openspec/changes/add-iphone-ble-client/tasks.md

iPhone BLE web controller tasks

Button implementation authorized (2026-10-20). Physical acceptance and publication remain separate gates. Proposal acceptance controls task 1.1; verification map defines H/P evidence. Bluefy delivery and button-first input are selected; the revised proposal is accepted for implementation by the explicit user answer recorded below. Check boxes only after their completion evidence passes.

1. Acceptance and environment

  • 1.1 Todor explicitly accepted in this conversation on 2026-10-20: “Accept proposal and implement buttons”, answering the question naming revised PR #95 and deferred accelerometer control. Acceptance record identifies the accepted commit. Product acceptance/publication/physical tests are not included.
  • 1.2 Record iPhone model/iOS/Bluefy version and required browser API/lifecycle feature checks; completion check: design.md records the proposed GitHub Pages route and identifies the delivery/phone observations still pending in I1–I4. No Mac, Xcode, signing credentials or membership is required for this web route.

2. Linux development and tests

  • 2.1 Implement codecs/capability/Status validation under apps/iphone; completion check: H1 Linux tests match existing Rust/Python vectors for 72-byte zero/six-direction setpoints, f32 limits, sequence wrap and malformed/boundary inputs. No firmware/API changes. H1: cd apps/iphone && npm test, 3 codec tests passed on Linux (2026-10-20).
  • 2.2 Implement the minimal static button UI and expiring intent policy; completion check: H4/H5 Linux browser tests cover six signs/caps, disabled axes, simultaneous touches, release/slide/cancel/lost capture, stalled UI renewal, 250 ms expiry, text/accessibility and no sticky sensor/accessibility input. Sensor APIs remain unused. Evidence: 4 Hold unit tests and 4 Chromium UI tests passed on Linux (2026-10-20).
  • 2.3 Implement the Web Bluetooth adapter with explicit picker/connect, feature/GATT validation and bounded setup; completion check: H2 exercises missing APIs, insecure origin, cancelled/late picker selection, invalid peer/zero-write rejection, claim loss, connect timeout and late completion without automatic recovery. Do not implement native scan/MTU/readiness APIs. H2: 4 transport, 3 session setup/picker/link-loss tests and the browser missing-API test passed on Linux (2026-10-20).
  • 2.4 Implement serialized GATT/control/Status work and periodic latest-intent transmission; completion check: H3 passes zero-before-ARM, read-promise-only confirmation, STOP priority, safety-stop latch, 200 ms gap/backpressure, read/control deadlines and stale-promise/event cases, with no queued motion. H3: 9 session tests passed on Linux (2026-10-20).
  • 2.5 Implement page/host interruption handling and bounded cleanup; completion check: H5 injects blur/hidden/pagehide/verified host inactivity, disconnect/error, reload and failed/hung writes, verifying disconnect attempted within 500 ms while runnable. README documents firmware fallback, browser evidence limits and the later input-interpreter boundary without implementing sensors. Active foreground and manual recovery H2/H5 (inactive/return/reload) P3 actual host events/frame expiry/termination
