Bluefy / normal product firmware evidence planned

These are proposed checks, not authorization to run them. No hosted page, phone, network, router, serial or motor activity occurred while revising this draft. Use normal default or ros firmware; never motor-bench. Do not change firmware to make Bluefy pass.

  • P1 — browser/claim/payload integration (I1/I2): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Record phone/iOS/Bluefy/web/firmware revisions, HTTPS origin, split with/without-response write APIs, explicit read promises/notifications, name-only picker and error behavior. Across 10 manual connections, verify validated setup and explicit ARM/STOP at zero with the expected fresh Status. The phone's 72-byte capability is user-confirmed; this checks our browser/firmware path. Record ATT MTU/capacity only if actually measured externally; unavailable MTU is not a browser failure or fabricated API result. Record claim timing and release observations separately.
  • P2 — full workload (I3/Q19): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Run 60 s at 20 Hz zero including Status polling and explicit ARM/STOP/re-arm at zero. Require no lease expiry, submission gap>=200 ms or one-second control/read timeout. Log pending-operation delays, promise durations, submission-gap distribution and read/control latency. Only actual instrumentation can establish connection interval; timer frequency/BlueZ cannot. Failing performance requires reviewed contract/approach changes before motor checks.
  • P3 — host lifecycle and usability (I1/I4): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Verify real pointer/hold/cancel/multi-touch, accessibility/text sizing, Bluefy browser controls, blur/page visibility, app switch/Home, lock/unlock, interruptions, Bluetooth off/on, permission changes, navigation, force termination/reload and unavailable peer. Record detected events, UI renewal expiry, last nonzero submission, cleanup attempts and device-reported state. P3 fails if an inactive host keeps renewing nonzero intent/streaming it; unsupported signals must not silently become a safety promise. Distinguish observed expiry/firmware fallback from runnable cleanup. Record non-inducible cases as unverified.
  • P4 — supervised wheel acceptance: only after P1–P3 and a separately announced batch with Todor's go, wheels off ground. Observe six directions briefly, release-to-zero, STOP during hold, new ARM/new press, lock/background and link loss. Record Todor's physical observations separately from browser/protocol/firmware logs. Confirm independent lease fallback; app deadlines are not physical stop bounds. No electrical/coast limits, floor speed accuracy, range or unattended-safety claim.

Record date, exact steps, hardware/browser/web/firmware identities, logs, observations and failures. Hardware policy and acceptance gates apply. Missing/failed evidence leaves its task unchecked; revised behavior returns to proposal review.

All 43 requirements have named software/review evidence; the physical results and skipped checks remain distinct below. No blocking implementation decision remains within this scope.

ROS All six scripts: ros-scenarios.sh, ros-router-gone.sh, ros-reconnect.sh, ros-refresh.sh, ros-stale-session.sh, ros-capabilities.sh (includes capabilities and status observers). Scripts run sequentially because three use the same host router port/container name. CI also runs the board runners for read-only delivery, ROS stop/recovery, router loss, shared UDP/ROS ownership and ROS device-clock lease timing on loopback ports 17449–17453. No hardware is involved.
Firmware Product and experiment: clippy/build for ESP32-S3, with and without ROS. Product no_std crates are linked into both firmware variants. Motor crate dependency inspection shows no dependencies.

The merged software through task 3.5 passed all four main checks. The audit added the three previously local-only ROS scripts and sim clippy without ROS. It also reproduced and fixed invalid motor configuration reporting a successful ARM before the coordinator tick: ARM now reports not-ready on every source, including before the first tick. No test-count or existence check alone proves scenario coverage; the rows describe the assertions reviewed.

The prepared UDP board probe reuses the product socket client. test_udp_probe_against_product_simulator runs all four stop/recovery scenarios on loopback; test_lost_cleanup_bye_cannot_report_released drops BYE and requires the probe to reject missing serial release. That regression failed first before adding the release assertion. These simulator checks alone do not count as physical acceptance. The subsequent authorized board batch passed protocol assertions and Todor confirmed all four wheel stops, pauses and recovery.

The prepared ROS read-only board batch reuses ros_capabilities.py and ros_status.py before/after a router restart. Loopback results: capabilities late receipt 0.551/0.620 s, Status 0.755/0.751 s, maximum observed period 0.909 s, ownership changes about 0.010 s; no arming. The subsequent authorized ROS board batch passed both probes before/after router restart: capabilities late receipt 0.574/0.667 s, Status 0.766/0.783 s, largest observed period 0.908 s, claim/release updates 0.011–0.031 s. The serial link rejoined in 2.083 s and never armed. Actual ESP32 capabilities/Status delivery passed; this read-only batch did not test motors.

The ROS motor batch prepares STOP, lease expiry and out-of-limits checks using one node's cmd_vel/arm publishers. Each stop/recovery requires fresh serial and canonical Status evidence. STOP/limits must inhibit fresh streaming until explicit ARM; ROS lease recovery auto-arms on resumed input as specified. The identical runner is exercised on loopback in CI; the subsequent authorized board batch passed every protocol/serial assertion. Todor confirmed all four wheel stops, pauses and explicit/automatic recoveries at vx=0.1 (“Yes, all as expected”). ROS owner/router loss while driving is prepared in ros_router_loss.sh (killed router: OwnerLost without lease stop; frozen router: lease stop, release and link-down), passing on loopback/CI. The board run passed both, and Todor confirmed all four wheels stopped and stayed still.

Physical evidence and deferrals

Task 5.2 disposition

On 2026-10-19 Todor instructed: “skip task 5.2 since we dont have good measurement tools”. Task 5.2 is closed with the completed evidence below retained and the remaining equipment-dependent checks skipped. Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband measurements and the coast/driven-neighbour check are deferred to a later change when suitable measurement tools are available. They have not passed physical validation; host pin-ordering and mapping tests remain software evidence only. No further board run is scheduled for task 5.2. This scope decision does not change the specified motor behavior. The task 5.3 review records acceptance within these limits.

Earlier product runs are development evidence: coordinator, validation and BLE reconnect. They used earlier firmware; they do not accept the current product. M4/M5 remain the comparison/rollback reference. Each physical motor run is announced separately and waits for Todor's go.

Check Required product evidence Task
Mapping and profile Compare all four direction/PWM channels and both STBY outputs with the carrier schematic; confirm 0.02 deadband, 40–70% drive range and no inversions. Then verify each physical wheel/direction. 5.1 source/net check complete; 5.2 physical wheel directions passed: all four wheels, both directions, forward/strafe/rotate confirmed by Todor; deadband/drive-range not separately measured
Boot/reset/power loss With motor power present, no unintended wheel movement on startup/reset or ESP32 power loss/recovery; record what was observed rather than infer pin levels from logs. 5.2 physical batch passed: two idle resets without twitch, all four wheels stopped at the driving reset and stayed still through reboot, and no movement on USB power loss/restoration; all four checks confirmed by Todor
Stops and recovery All four wheels stop on STOP, lease expiry, BLE disconnect, UDP BYE, ROS owner/router loss and out-of-limits. Verify retained/released owner and fresh-input/explicit-ARM recovery rules; check lease detection within lease + 50 ms using client/serial timing. 5.2 BLE physical subset passed: STOP/lease/out-of-limits plus pauses/recovery confirmed by Todor; BLE owner-loss physical repeat passed, all four stopped and disarmed reconnect confirmed by Todor; UDP four-stop physical batch passed, including fresh-stream inhibition and explicit recovery; ROS three-stop physical batch passed, including STOP/limits inhibition and explicit recovery plus automatic lease recovery; ROS router-loss physical batch passed (killed: OwnerLost; frozen: lease stop then release/link-down); UDP lease timing passed on board: five conservative upper bounds 1,006.483–1,015.314 ms, all below 1,050 ms, zero wheel commands, unsolicited Status and release; Todor confirmed all four wheels stayed still throughout; BLE device-clock timing passed after the authorized instrumented ROS flash: five lateness values 7/4/4/4/2 ms, each ≤ 50 ms, with fresh lease Status and cleanup release; Todor confirmed all four wheels stayed still through flash/boot/trials/cleanup. The earlier failed host-bound attempt remains preserved for its original build. ROS device-clock timing passed: five lateness values 4/9/2/5/4 ms, each ≤ 50 ms, with matching ROS Status in one session and cleanup release; Todor confirmed all four wheels stayed still through reset/trials/cleanup. Router/firewall cleanup and Wi-Fi restoration completed
Coast and neighbour Documented zero-wheel pin levels (PWM high, directions low), free rotation and a driven neighbour remaining enabled. A hand-spin alone does not prove pin levels. Coast distance is not claimed. 5.2 Skipped/deferred by Todor, 2026-10-19: no suitable measurement tools; not physically validated. See task disposition.
Radio and delivery Actual BLE/AP exclusion and recovery; shared Wi-Fi owner isolation; immediate BLE Status reads and changed notifications; UDP stop notifications; ROS capabilities/status and router recovery. BLE Status/Echo subset passed on 7c2e2df, including empty/4/32-byte Echo, immediate reads and changed Status notifications. UDP board delivery passed unsolicited stop Status and second-endpoint exclusion; ROS read-only board delivery passed capabilities/Status before and after router restart; ROS router recovery while driving passed; BLE/AP exclusion and recovery passed (BLE owner makes the AP unjoinable; UDP owner stops advertising; both recover on release); UDP/ROS shared-AP exclusion passed in both directions (no intruder claim, drive or lease renewal; AP stayed on), with all four wheels confirmed still by Todor. 5.2
Reversal and heat Product motor module at the 70% cap: direct full reversals on all four, owner/radio survives with no reset; supervised thermal run. Use a motor-module bench harness for full-scale vectors; do not raise API limits to force full duty. 5.2 reversal batch prepared: opt-in full-scale vectors through the product motor module/coordinator, ten direct reversals, UDP session/radio checks and normal-image restoration; host/loopback checks pass. The first board attempt aborted at zero due to a host log-prefix bug, now reproduced/fixed in replay tests; normal firmware restored and all wheels confirmed still through both flashes/boots and cleanup. That attempt did not perform a reversal. The separately authorized repeat passed physically: ten direct all-wheel reversals at the configured 70% cap, same UDP session/radio surviving, final zero/STOP/release, no unplanned reboot/product fault/panic/drop, and normal ROS firmware restored. Todor confirmed all directions, final stop and still wheels through both flashes/boots; network restored/captures stopped. Electrical pin/duty measurements were not made; the endurance/heating result follows below. A five-minute visual stand endurance batch is prepared with accelerated socket checks and a mid-hold STOP negative control; the first attempt aborted at the unarmed announcement timeout before probe launch, with no claim/arming. Normal firmware/network restored, captures stopped, and all wheels confirmed still through flashes/boots/cleanup. The authorized repeat passed serial/session and physical checks: 300,093 ms of sustained full-forward demand, same UDP session, clean stop/release and normal-firmware/network restoration. Todor confirmed continuous motion of all four wheels for the full five minutes, the final stop and still wheels through both flashes/boots. He reported no warming in either drivers or motors: the qualitative supervised stand endurance/heating check passed for this run. No numeric temperature bounds, thermal margin, current or loaded-operation result is claimed
Acceptance Reconcile these results with every requirement; record acceptance and update instructions before archive. 5.3 Complete within the recorded scope, 2026-10-19: acceptance review; measurement deferrals remain unverified.

Deferred outside this change: start/stall current or current protection, operation above 70%, a numeric GPIO disable bound (O4), coast distance and measured maximum speeds. These are not missing host tests or implicit product claims; the equipment/scope decisions are in the proposal.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-laptop-teleoperation/verification.md

Laptop teleoperation verification

Application accepted for supervised stand use, 2026-10-20. Todor selected laptop teleoperation after #89 presented the scope, then separately authorized the announced board batch and explicitly confirmed its wheel results. Host failure tests and physical observations remain separate evidence. All tasks are complete; measurement deferrals and loaded/floor exclusions remain.

Run from the repository root:

python3 -m unittest discover -s apps/teleop/tests -t . -v

31 client tests cover protocol/policy assertions, real pseudo-terminals and fake peers, and the real client against the product simulator. Existing codec compatibility passed 23 Python tests, 40 bench tests and 14 UDP scenarios. These are host results, not electrical or radio qualification.

Requirement Actual host evidence Task
Explicit connection without motion ProtocolTests.test_handshake_is_single_and_validates_caps, test_invalid_floats_and_window_bounds_are_refused, test_busy_and_zero_session_fail, test_invalid_frames_do_not_refresh_deadline; TerminalTests.test_non_tty_and_invalid_target_never_connect checks no extra claim. The startup part of test_real_cli_start_arm_expiry_space_rearm_and_restore observes zero/no ARM before R. 2.2, 4.1
Explicit arm and stop latch PolicyTests.test_no_implicit_arm_and_new_direction_after_arm, test_reported_stop_and_errors_cancel_motion; real CLI Space latch/re-arm in TerminalTests.test_real_cli_start_arm_expiry_space_rearm_and_restore. 3.1, 3.2, 4.1
Gentle planar directions PolicyTests.test_all_six_signs_and_latest_only, test_zero_and_smaller_limits; SimulatorTests.test_six_directions_expiry_stop_latch_and_cleanup checks all six actual simulator wheel-sign patterns. 3.1, 4.1
Input expiry and latest intent PolicyTests.test_expiry_boundary_repeat_and_unrelated_keys, test_stop_and_quit_dominate_batch_and_clear_arm; simulator integration checks zero after every input expiry. 3.1, 3.2

The client schedules 50 ms ticks; simulator expiry and session survival exercise the real stream. 3.1, 3.2

Link checks without automatic recovery ProtocolTests.test_echo_nonce_session_and_age_are_independent; TerminalTests.test_lost_echo_exits_and_restores_without_reclaim, test_missing_arm_reply_fails_without_nonzero; SimulatorTests.test_killed_simulator_ends_client_without_reconnect kills an armed/driving simulator and observes client failure. 3.2, 4.1

Test sources: protocol, policy, runtime, terminal, simulator.

Physical acceptance — tasks 5.1/5.2

The separately authorized stand batch passed on the installed normal ROS firmware, without flashing. The actual terminal client performed five seconds idle, unarmed W, R at zero, six gentle directions with input-expiry pauses, forward/Space, unarmed W, explicit re-arm, fresh forward and Ctrl-D. Serial confirmed all six wheel patterns, zero at each pause, matching control acknowledgements and final STOP/release/Open. Capture stopped, previous Wi-Fi was restored and the internet route was unchanged. Todor confirmed: “Yes, all behaved as expected.” This includes all directions, every stop and still wheels through reset/startup and both unarmed checks.

This accepts the implemented application for supervised stand use. Malformed packets, refused/missing controls, lost links and scheduling failures remain covered by host tests; they were not injected into this physical batch. M6’s measurement deferrals remain unchanged; no electrical coast/STBY, current, temperature margin or loaded/floor result is claimed.

Shared codec container regression

The first #90 ROS CI run failed because the scenario compatibility import was mounted at /scenarios without the extracted apps/client package. The existing apps/simcar/scenarios/ros-capabilities.sh test reproduced IndexError: 3 locally before the fix. All three affected runners now mount scenarios and the shared codec in their repository layout inside the container. The same capabilities and reconnect test passes, as do ros_readonly.sh and default ros_stops.sh against loopback ROS simulators. The 31 client tests pass again. Firmware and UDP wire behavior are unchanged.

openspec/changes/add-iphone-ble-client/proposal.md

iPhone BLE web controller proposal

Why

Rovi's vision includes an iPhone controller, but the accepted product has only laptop clients. Todor has Linux, no Mac or Apple Developer Program membership, and prefers no subscription. A browser controller can use the existing BLE API without building or signing a new iOS app; see roadmap Q9/Q18/Q19.

What Changes

  • Target an HTTPS web controller opened in the free Bluefy iPhone browser, selected by Todor in this conversation. Standard Safari is not a supported BLE host. Develop and test the web code from Linux; no Xcode, native scaffold or signing workflow.
  • Use browser-mediated explicit device selection/connect, visible capabilities and last-reported Status. Connect disarmed; require fresh zero then explicit ARM before six gentle press-and-hold directions become usable.
  • Buttons are the selected first input method. Keep input interpretation separate from the bounded motion/session policy so a later accelerometer/tilt input can use the same limits, ARM, STOP and expiry rules. Sensor control, sensor permissions and calibration are deferred, not implemented in v1.
  • Bound hold age, stream stalls and cleanup. Page/host interruption or link failure clears motion; no automatic reconnect, re-arm or motion replay. Validate Bluefy's lifecycle behavior on the actual phone before accepting control.
  • Todor confirms the phone can send the 72-byte payload. Retain runtime failure handling and separate browser/firmware integration evidence from that user-reported phone capability; no new MTU measurement is claimed. Streaming-rate Q19 remains open.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • iphone-ble-teleoperation: iPhone browser discovery/selection, ownership, explicit arming, touch control, interruption handling and honest feedback through the existing BLE interface.

Modified Capabilities

None. Car control API, motor control and laptop teleoperation retain their accepted contracts.

Impact

Future implementation would be static HTML/CSS/JavaScript under apps/iphone/, using Web Bluetooth in Bluefy with no third-party runtime scripts or command server. Propose repository GitHub Pages hosting; verify the final origin/HTTPS during delivery. Existing normal product firmware (default or ros, never motor-bench), GATT UUIDs and codecs remain unchanged. BLE connection itself claims ownership and switches off the car AP; a picker alone does not claim. Missing advertisements do not prove another owner exists.

Specification PR #95 contains planning Markdown only; the button controller lands in a stacked implementation PR under apps/iphone/. Neither publishes hosting, runs device/network tests or changes firmware. Native iOS build/signing, Wi-Fi diagnostics, station mode, BLE credential provisioning (Q21), compact setpoints, pairing/authentication changes, background driving, mixed-axis controls and sensor driving are outside v1.

Proposal acceptance

Accepted for button-based implementation (2026-10-20). In this conversation Todor answered the explicit proposal question with: “Accept proposal and implement buttons”. This accepts the revised Bluefy requirements in PR #95 at b80e673a085d84c6d6dcd87c031194b5e7912bf4, with accelerometer control deferred. Task 1.1 records that evidence. Product/phone/wheel acceptance remains pending; no deployment or physical test is claimed or authorized by this record. Parent retains merge coordination. Implementation proceeds on the stacked feat/iphone-ble-web branch.

Review the design/OPEN questions, requirements, tasks and verification map. Implementation progress and evidence are tracked there; physical acceptance remains pending.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/proposal.md

M6: low-level four-wheel API

Status: archived/synced 2026-10-20 after #87 merged in f5a2d8e; proposed 2026-10-10; laptop implementation scope accepted 2026-10-17 by Todor's merge of #48. Open items O1–O8 closed or deferred 2026-10-17. Scoped product acceptance is recorded on 2026-10-19 in the task 5.3 review, using Todor’s physical confirmations and explicit task 5.2 measurement deferrals. The product crates, sim car and firmware are implemented; laptop conformance and CI are tracked in tasks 1–3. Existing experiments remain the comparison/rollback reference; unverified physical limits below remain explicit. Terms are as defined in GLOSSARY.md.

Why

VISION layer 2 needs a product API that drives the car's four wheels independently, stays independent of transport and mecanum math, and fails safe. M8 (README) proved the transport and ownership model on the board. M4 added four physical motor outputs and verified stops, reversals and a thermal run; M5 demonstrated floor movement and recorded approximate motion references. This change turns that experimental behavior into a reusable product API, separating motor control from the device state machine. It reuses the working code and evidence rather than starting another firmware experiment.

What Changes

  • motor-control (new): the reusable layer that takes four wheel commands (FL, FR, RR, RL, normalised −1..1) and drives the motor drivers. It knows nothing of setpoints, kinematics or transports. It owns driver standby, the boot-safe state and the limits M4 measures.
  • car-control-api (new): the car's device control API, extracted from M8 with its explicit transport differences (including ROS auto-arm). This proposal corrects validation, ordering, fault recovery and status gaps described in the design; it does not claim behavior-identical extraction.
  • Firmware integration follows the accepted laptop implementation tasks; flashing and motor runs require separate authorization. BLE/UDP byte layouts and numeric codes stay as M8 defines them (README); this spec states behaviour, not wire formats.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • motor-control: independent wheel commands, driver standby, duty limits and fault handling.
  • car-control-api: setpoint processing, ownership, arming, lease, capabilities and status.

Modified Capabilities

None; this is the first product specification change.

Design decisions

  • The motor control boundary is normalised wheel commands, not SI wheel speeds. M5 confirmed no encoders; the current car uses open-loop duty control (Q11/O3, 2026-10-17). A normalised command survives both: 1.0 means the configured maximum, whether that is a duty or a wheel speed. The device layer still converts setpoints to SI wheel speeds first, as mecanum_drive_controller does (ADR-0006).
  • Controllers cannot send wheel commands directly. The device control API accepts setpoints only. Exposing four wheel velocities stays deferred, as ADR-0006 records; motor control is a firmware-internal boundary.
  • ROS 2 controllers read capabilities before claiming. A ROS 2 controller claims with its first setpoint, so it needs the limits before it claims. The car publishes /rovi/capabilities (std_msgs/String, key=value) without a claim. O9 selected the specified reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback: changes plus a 900 ms heartbeat; retained history was unavailable with the pinned publisher. Rejected: a custom message type (every controller must build a Rovi interface package) and ROS 2 parameters (they need services, which the car does not serve).
  • Safety is enforced twice. The device layer raises safety stops (ADR-0004); motor control independently holds standby until it is explicitly enabled and on any invalid wheel command.

Implementation boundaries, migration and the reviewed contract changes are in design.md. Existing ADRs remain authoritative; no new irreversible architectural decision is introduced.

Evidence and remaining decisions

Use M4 results, M5 results and the accepted motion references. Todor stopped the extended measurement sweep; no new motor tests are queued by this proposal. Approximate references are not guaranteed velocity tracking.

ID Status Answer
O1 Closed 2026-10-17 Duty limits stay configurable. The product profile caps drive duty at 70%, the envelope M4 verified on the bench (ten ±70% reversals, 5-minute thermal run, radio up). The experiment firmware's 100% is not a product value. Deferred, needs a current monitor (INA226) or an oscilloscope with a shunt: start and stall current. Needed only to raise the cap or to claim current protection; this change claims neither.
O2 Closed 2026-10-17 Measured geometry: radius 0.030 m, wheelbase 0.115 m, track 0.140 m, centre projection sum 0.1275 m. Open-loop with the accepted approximate motion references; no calibration sweep. The 40 rad/s normalization and 1/1/3 input limits stay in the profile, labelled experimental, not measured maxima. The references were recorded on the experiment's 40–100% mapping; under the 70% cap the same command gives less duty (vx 0.20: 45% instead of 50%). Maximum physical speeds are not claimed.
O3 Closed Open-loop duty control; no encoders, added sensing out of scope.
O4 Deferred, needs a logic analyzer or oscilloscope A numeric pin-level STBY disable bound. This change specifies and host-tests that a safety stop deasserts both STBY outputs in the control tick that processes it, before any further bridge update. M4 observed all four wheels stop on every trigger. No numeric bound is claimed.
O5 Closed 2026-10-17 Coast for an individual zero wheel (TB6612 IN1=IN2=low, PWM=high), standby for every safety stop. The experiment's all-low zero pins do not prove coast; task 2.1 corrects them test-first. Coast distance is not measured or claimed (tape and video, if a later requirement needs it).
O6 Closed Exact zero and magnitudes below 0.02 coast; other commands map linearly from 40% to the configured maximum. About 35% starting duty observed on the stand; no per-wheel threshold is claimed.
O7 Closed 2026-10-17 Direct reversals, no ramp, up to the 70% cap: M4's ten ±70% reversals caused no ESP32 reset or BLE loss. Raising the cap reopens O7 together with O1.
O8 Closed D1 A→FL, D1 B→RL, D2 A→FR, D2 B→RR; directions corrected at connectors, all software inversions false, reconfirmed after the motor rework. Each driver has its own STBY, both disabled on a safety stop.
O9 Closed 2026-10-17 The pinned ordinary publisher did not serve history to a late Jazzy transient-local subscriber (no sample within 3 s; its later live sample arrived). Selected the specified reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback: every 900 ms (headroom under one second), on claim/release and reconnect. Late subscribers received in 0.413/0.551 s before/after router restart; probe and fallback evidence.

On 2026-10-19 Todor closed task 5.2 with the remaining equipment-dependent checks skipped because suitable measurement tools are unavailable. Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband measurements and the coast/driven-neighbour check remain physically unverified; they return in a later change with suitable tools. Completed board results are retained in the verification map; task 5.3 records acceptance within that scope. Specified motor behavior is unchanged.

No unresolved product decisions remain. Deferred items are outside this change: it does not claim measured current, a numeric disable bound, coast distance, maximum speeds or operation above 70%. Equipment-gated items return as a new change when the equipment is available. Retain the experiment firmware for comparison; product acceptance is a separate checklist.

First implementation scope

  • Reuse M8's core, motor mapping and tests in a shared Cargo workspace; isolate motor control from the arbiter and transports.
  • Add conformance tests for the specified deadband/duty rule, independent wheels, faults, standby and documented zero-output mode.
  • Keep BLE, UDP, optional ROS and the accepted ownership/arming policies. Apply the reviewed corrections and implement the agreed ROS capabilities and extended status topics.
  • No new encoder, camera, phone-app, station-mode or hardware-monitor work in this change.
  • Do not flash or start a motor test as part of extraction or host validation. Each board run is announced separately and waits for Todor's go.

Impact

  • Planning: openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/, following the product specification standard and ADR-0015.
  • Code: crates/rovi-core, crates/rovi-motor-control and crates/rovi-drive in the root workspace, with separate apps/simcar and firmware packages/lockfiles. The tasks and verification map record software checks, confirmed board results and explicit physical deferrals.
  • Evidence: host tests and the sim car are development evidence only (ADR-0002). The scoped acceptance review uses the product board runs linked in the verification map, preserving M4/M5 as references.

Review status

The 2026-10-17 review findings are addressed: ROS latch exceptions, complete motor fault/configuration recovery, clamped kinematics, shared Wi-Fi exclusion, explicit transport edge cases and ROS field/QoS contracts. The design and verification map accompany the requirements. Todor merged #48 on 2026-10-17, accepting the laptop implementation tasks (task 1.1). That does not establish product hardware acceptance or authorize a flash/motor run. The same day Todor agreed O1 and O2; O5 and O7 closed with them, and O4 and O1's current measurement are deferred as equipment-gated. O9 closed with the specified volatile fallback and recorded Jazzy evidence.

The 2026-10-19 final acceptance review completes task 5.3 for the recorded scope. It preserves the equipment-dependent checks Todor skipped as physically unverified; no new qualification claims or motor authorization follow from acceptance. The pinned CLI archived/synced this change on 2026-10-20 after the stack landed, creating the car control API and motor control baselines without changing requirement behavior. Measurements explicitly deferred at acceptance remain unverified.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-laptop-teleoperation/proposal.md

Laptop UDP teleoperation

Status: implemented and accepted for supervised stand use on 2026-10-20. Todor selected the laptop scope, separately authorized the announced board batch, and confirmed all directions, stops and still phases. Archived/synced through the pinned CLI on 2026-10-20; accepted requirements. Each future motor batch still needs its own announced go.

Why

The vision calls for teleoperation above the device API. M6 now provides that API, but the laptop tools are scenario/bench runners rather than an interactive product client.

What Changes

  • Add a Linux terminal client over the existing UDP protocol: explicit target, connect disarmed, explicit arm, six gentle directions, STOP and quit.
  • Bound each recognized motion key to a 250 ms input window; stream zeros when input expires, and clear motion on STOP, faults or communication failure. No automatic claim/re-arm after failure.
  • Reuse the tested TwistStamped, capability and Status codecs. Add deterministic policy tests, simulated UDP peers and product-simulator coverage before any separately authorized board test.
  • Preserve M6’s firmware, ownership, wire codes, lease and 70% product cap. No iPhone/BLE client, ROS controller, station mode, floor/autonomous behavior or new physical qualification claim in this change.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • laptop-teleoperation: interactive laptop input, client-side arming, bounded command streaming, status presentation and shutdown over the existing UDP API.

Modified Capabilities

None. The client consumes car-control-api; it does not alter that contract or motor-control.

Impact

  • Code: a small standard-library Python client under apps/teleop, a shared codec module, simulator tests and product usage instructions. No additional runtime dependency.
  • Existing Python wire-codec callers retain compatibility; Rust/firmware and experimental behavior remain unchanged.
  • Product implementation requires explicit proposal acceptance per SPECIFICATION. Each motor batch remains separately announced and authorized. M6’s measurement deferrals remain in effect.

Scope choice

Todor selected laptop UDP teleoperation on 2026-10-20. The proposed keys, gentle defaults and bounded-input policy define this reversible first client; Q9 and Q21 remain separate future work.

Implementation progress

The laptop client is implemented under apps/teleop, using shared apps/client payload codecs with the former import path preserved. Host protocol/policy, pseudo-terminal, fake-peer and product-simulator tests are linked in the verification map. CI includes the client suite. The separate stand batch passed on 2026-10-20 with Todor’s explicit wheel observations (evidence). The application is accepted for this supervised stand scope; no new measurement, firmware change, flash or loaded/floor result is claimed.

Generated from OpenSpec Markdown. Make changes in the source, then run npm run spec:build. This reader does not approve a proposal or authorize hardware tests.
